title: True words, false speakers.
subtitle: When the sentence is right but the heart is not
then: In Madinah some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and declared that he was Allah's Messenger. The statement was true. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they did not believe inwardly what they declared outwardly{/trap}, so Allah Himself testified that they were lying.
now: You say "inshallah" when you have no plan to come. You type "praying for you" and never pray. You say "I believe" in a gathering where everyone is watching. {idea}Allah listens to what is underneath the sentence.{/idea}
old: As long as I say the right things, I am fine.
new: Even true words are a lie if I do not mean them inside.
try: The next time you say "I will pray for you" today, stop and actually make that dua right then.

title: They used their oaths as a shield.
subtitle: Swearing by Allah to hide behind Him
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites shielded themselves by {trap}falsely swearing to be what they were not{/trap}. Some Muslims trusted them and even copied them, which led people away from Allah's path. When Abdullah bin Ubayy was confronted, he too swore he had said nothing.
now: Your manager asks if you sent the report. Your mum asks if you took the money. "Wallahi, I did." {trap}Allah's name becomes a wall to hide behind.{/trap} {idea}His name is not a tool to win an argument.{/idea}
old: Swearing by Allah is just a strong way to be believed.
new: Using Allah's name to cover a lie turns the holiest word into a hiding place.
try: Go one full day without saying wallahi casually. Save it for when it truly matters.

title: They believed, then disbelieved, and their hearts were sealed.
subtitle: A heart closes after it turns back
then: Ibn Kathir explains that they {trap}exchanged guidance for misguidance{/trap}, reverting from faith to disbelief. Because of that, their hearts were stamped so that they could no longer grasp guidance. {idea}The seal came after the choice.{/idea}
now: You used to cry in taraweeh. Then you started skipping, then mocking a little, then not caring. Now the Quran feels like noise. {idea}It did not go dark in a day.{/idea} {reward}A heart that still worries about this is not sealed.{/reward}
old: I just do not feel anything when I hear the Quran anymore.
new: Hearts close step by step after turning away, and they open the same way.
try: Listen to one short surah today with the translation, slowly, and let yourself feel whatever comes.

title: Impressive bodies, smooth words, propped-up wood.
subtitle: Looking solid and being solid are different
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites had {trap}a graceful look and eloquent speech{/trap}, yet inside they were weak and full of fear. Like wood leaning on a wall, they had shape but no substance. {trap}Every alarm made them think it was coming for them.{/trap}
now: The feed is full of people who look perfect and talk well. You start polishing your own image too: the outfit, the caption, the confident voice in meetings. {idea}Ask what is holding you up from inside.{/idea} {trap}Image without substance is always nervous.{/trap}
old: If I look good and speak well, people will respect me.
new: A strong inside matters more than a polished outside, and it is calmer too.
try: Spend the time you would spend on one post or outfit today on two rakahs no one sees.

title: Come, be forgiven. They turned their heads away.
subtitle: Pride that refuses an open door
then: Ibn Ishaq reports that after Uhud, Abdullah bin Ubayy was stopped from speaking in the mosque. Some Ansar told him to go back so the Messenger ﷺ could ask forgiveness for him. {trap}He said he did not want that.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they turned away in arrogance, belittling what they were offered.
now: Your brother says, "just call Dad and say sorry, he will forgive you." You know he is right. {trap}You turn your face away anyway.{/trap} {idea}The door is open. Only pride is standing in it.{/idea}
old: Asking for forgiveness would make me look weak.
new: The door to forgiveness was open, and only my pride kept it shut.
try: Send one short apology today that you have been putting off out of pride.

title: Asking for them or not, it is the same.
subtitle: Forgiveness cannot reach a heart that refuses it

row.title: I turn myself
sub: no one can do it for me

then: Because they turned away in pride, Allah said it made no difference whether the Prophet ﷺ prayed for them or not. Ibn Kathir notes a similar verse in Surah Bara'ah. {trap}Allah does not guide those who keep rebelling.{/trap}
now: You ask your mother to make dua for you, you ask the imam, you hope someone's prayers will carry you. {idea}They help, and they are a gift.{/idea} {reward}But the one turning back to Allah has to be you.{/reward}
old: If enough good people pray for me, I will be fine.
new: Others' prayers help, but forgiveness needs my own turning back.
try: Say astaghfirullah ten times today in your own words, not waiting for anyone to say it for you.

title: Stop feeding them, and they will leave him.
subtitle: They thought they held the purse strings
then: On the journey back from Bani al-Mustaliq, Abdullah bin Ubayy told the Ansar they had shared their wealth with the emigrants and that {trap}if they stopped, the emigrants would have to leave{/trap}. Allah replied that {reward}the treasures of heaven and earth belong to Him{/reward}.
now: A boss hints your contract depends on staying quiet. A relative reminds you who paid for the wedding. {trap}Money starts to feel like the one who decides your life.{/trap} {reward}Every treasury belongs to Allah.{/reward}
old: Whoever pays me controls what I can and cannot do.
new: My provision comes from Allah, whoever's hand it passes through.
try: Next time money tempts you to stay silent about something wrong, say quietly: the treasures are His.

title: Honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.
subtitle: Who is really the mighty one
then: Two men fought over water and shouted for their tribes. The Prophet ﷺ called it {trap}a call of ignorance, offensive{/trap}. Ibn Ubayy then said the mightier would expel the weaker from Madinah. Usayd bin Hudayr told the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}you are the mighty one{/reward}, and Allah confirmed honor is His and the believers'.
now: A football argument becomes "your lot always". A family feud becomes "people from your side". {trap}The old tribal shout comes out quickly.{/trap} {idea}Honor is not your surname, your country, or your crowd.{/idea}
old: My group is better, and people should know their place.
new: Real honor comes from Allah, and He gives it to believers, not to tribes.
try: Next time you feel an "us versus them" thought about other Muslims, stop and make dua for them instead.

title: Do not let wealth and children distract you from Allah.
subtitle: Good things can still pull you away
then: After describing the hypocrites, the surah turns to the believers. Ibn Kathir says Allah tells them not to be {trap}distracted from His remembrance by indulging in property and children excessively{/trap}. Those who are busied away from what they were created for are {trap}the losers{/trap}.
now: Your days are full of good things: providing for the family, homework, swimming lessons, overtime. Then you realise you have not prayed with focus in weeks. {idea}The blessings were meant to be with Allah, not instead of Him.{/idea}
old: I am busy with my family and job, so Allah will understand.
new: Even my family and work should not push out remembering Allah.
try: Pray one prayer today with your children, or with them nearby, so the blessing and the remembrance meet.

title: Give now, before you beg for one more moment.
subtitle: The wish everyone makes at the end
then: Allah tells believers to spend from what He gave them before death comes. Ibn Kathir says {trap}everyone who fell short will regret it at death and ask for a short delay{/trap} to do better. The wish the verse quotes is specific: to give charity.
now: You keep meaning to set up that monthly donation. You will do it after the car is paid off, after the raise, after the move. {trap}The person in the verse said the same.{/trap} {reward}Give the small amount you have today.{/reward}
old: I will give more when I have more to spare.
new: The thing people wish for at death is to have given, so I give now.
try: Give any small amount to charity today, even the change in your pocket.

title: When the time comes, no soul is delayed.
subtitle: There is no extension on the appointed hour
then: The surah ends after the wish for one more moment. Ibn Kathir says that {trap}when the time of death comes, no one is given respite{/trap}. What happened has happened. And {idea}Allah is fully aware of what you do{/idea}, so the deeds are what count.
now: Your calendar is full of things you will do next month. {trap}None of them are promised.{/trap} {idea}You cannot add a minute to your life, but you can choose what goes into the minutes you have.{/idea}
old: There will always be time to sort things out later.
new: My time is fixed, so what matters is how I fill what is left of it.
try: Pick the one good thing you keep saying "next month" about, and do the first step today.
